description: Linter. A linter looks for errors in code. It does not start the program. The linter reads the code like a text. It knows many common error patterns. For example: a variable is never used. Or a name is spelled wrong. The linter reports such spots right away. A test is something else. A test really starts the program. A formatter is also something else. It only makes the code neat and pretty. The linter checks the content instead.
example: Think of a proofreader for a cookbook. He reads all the recipes closely. He finds spelling mistakes and missing ingredients. But he does not cook a single dish. A linter works with code the same way.
